newsitem.title: GERMANY: ECB must not use reserve requirement - German banks.
newsitem.headline: ECB must not use reserve requirement - German banks.

text.p: A German bank association on Friday reiterated its opposition to the use of minimum reserves as a policy tool for the future European Central Bank (ECB).

The Federal Association of German Banks said a minimum reserve requirement was superfluous, would be harmful to financial centres in the future Euro currency area and would make it harder for the ECB to conduct monetary policy.
The association praised the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the forereunner of the ECB, for publishing the range of monetary policy tools which the ECB can choose from when it starts work in 1999.

"Banks now have enough time to prepare for the way in which central bank money will be made available in future, even though the decision on important questions will be left up to the central council of the ECB," the group said in a statement.

The EMI made clear on Friday that the final decisions on several key outstanding issues -- such as whether the ECB will impose minimum reserves on banks as desired by the Bundesbank -- will have to be made by the ECB itself.

The association also praised the EMI for arranging a set of money policy tools that concentrated on open market operations with a broad range of banks, thereby ensuring that monetary policy corresponded with market conditions.
The association represent private sector banks in Germany.
